newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude rises, trade slows as August fades out.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude rises, trade slows as August fades out.

text.p: Crude prices in the U.S. firmed on Friday in a futures-led rally, while physical trading of domestic grades dwindled as market players turned to September business.
September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was around 30 cents higher at $20.00 a barrel, with August quoted 25/20 cents under September.
The rise was largely attributed to the gasoline rally in the New York Harbor which has been driven by short-covering and speculative buying because of some August supply shortages and firm demand.
However, traders said that looking forward there were more bearish forces likely to come into play.

"There's very little August left to do. Everyone is looking ahead to September and it really looks like it's got some room to drop there," said a trader for a medium-sized integrated oil company in the SouthWest.
Among Friday's trades, Midland/West Texas Intermediate traded at 30 cents under benchmark WTI, about two-to-three cents deeper discount than on Thursday.
Dealers said Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was still quoted either side of evens having traded there on Thursday late, with September at around 22-25 cents premium.
Sour crudes saw West Texas Sour/Midland talk at $1.65-70 under September WTI, about five cents weaker on the day.
Postings Plus for September closed traded from $1.93 to $1.97, steady from around $1.93-95 late yesterday, reflecting a September firming slightly to five cents.
